newsitem.title: UK: Britain launches wide-ranging pensions review.
newsitem.headline: Britain launches wide-ranging pensions review.

text.p: Social Security Secretary Harriet Harman on Wednesday announced plans for a wide-ranging review of the British pensions system which would "establish the right balance between the public and private sectors".
The review will include consideration of how the government can take forward proposals for new "Stakeholder Pensions" which it pledged to set up in its election manifesto, she said.

Government sources said the new pensions, to be provided by an alliance of employer and employee organisations and financial services companies, would meet the needs of people on modest incomes or in changing employment patterns.
They could also provide a vehicle for smaller firms to make pensions provision for their employees, they said.
The sources said the government hopes to complete the review in time to introduce pensions legislation in the current session of parliament, which is expected to last until late 2001 or early 2002.

The Labour government is committed to continuing the State Earnings Related Pension Scheme (SERPS), but, conscious of the challenge of providing pensions for an ageing population, wants to encourage as many people as possible to have an occupational or private pension.
"We recognise that for many people security in retirement can best be achieved by building up their own funded second pension," Harman said.

She said the Stakeholder pensions would "offer secure, flexible and value-for-money pensions for those who cannot join an employer's occupational scheme, whose pay is low or intermittent and for whom personal pensions are usually unsuitable."
Harman said the review would also look into the development of Citizenship Pensions for carers unable to contribute to pensions in their own right. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
